claims.text: Molecular dynamics simulations can investigate the thermal behavior of AuCoCuNiPt nanoparticles at the atomic scale.
In situ transmission electron microscopy can investigate the thermal behavior of AuCoCuNiPt nanoparticles at the atomic scale.
The nanoparticles are considered in their as-synthesized state.
The proposed intervention is heating or cooling the nanoparticles to various temperatures.
Atomic structure and composition are the structural variables proposed to mediate the thermal response.
Temperature changes are predicted to produce changes in the atomic structure of the nanoparticles.
Temperature changes are predicted to produce changes in the composition of the nanoparticles.
The mechanism is said to derive from general materials-science principles rather than evidence transferred to AuCoCuNiPt.
The initial atomic structure and composition provide the baseline for comparison.
The relevant boundary consists of the investigated temperature range and timescale.
The accuracy of molecular dynamics simulations or in situ TEM measurements is a source of uncertainty.
Observing no temperature-induced change in atomic structure or composition would falsify the hypothesis.
